claim: Eight of 235 functions in the head map package _authz/served.py (member name served.py, staged, two pins: 361c44fa9d and 74a62fb46c). None of the eight pinned blobs carries the AR-y-172 status rule; the head blob does. Narrative's tests run its staged pinned copy and cannot see the rule. The other seven test suites import the head _authz/served.py, which carries the rule, while their shipped bytes do not.
not_read: No function was run, deployed, invoked or called; no AWS, network or push.

Only the import and sys.path wiring of each test folder was read, not every test body; the suites were not executed.
The worktree copy of lambda-source-map.json (blob 78e79160) and of _authz/served.py (blob 1d55a27a) are older than the read ref and were not used.

Between the worktree copy and the read ref, 17 map entries differ, all eight of the packagers among them, in their loaders.py pins and artifact_sha256 values; the served.py rows of the eight are the same in both. The other 9 differing entries were not examined.
Prose notes in the other 227 entries were searched for served mentions, not read in full.
what_moves_together: For one internal caller to get one answer from all eight, one served.py that carries the AR-y-172 status rule (the head blob cf1091b454 or a later pin of it) must be the member every one of the eight stages: the map rows for served.py at 361c44fa9d (performance-adapter, narrative, status) and 74a62fb46c (directory-search, ycharts-generate, export-render, holdings, 49f-reporting-read-lambda) move together to that pin, each function is rebuilt and redeployed in the same window, and narrative's test staging reads the new pin so its suite stops running the old bytes. The seven live-testing suites already import the head file that carries the rule, so their suites run it while their shipped bytes do not; no test edit is needed for them to run it. Any other shared member the head served.py depends on at its pin (errors.py, enforce.py) must be the same version in each function's staged set.
